slides.title: Platforms must act in **2 hours.**
slides.body: If you (or someone for you) complain, a platform must take all reasonable steps within 2 hours to remove or disable content showing your private area, nudity, a sexual act, or morphed images of you.
slides.ref: IT Rules 2021 · Rule 3(2)(b), as amended 10 Feb 2026

slides.title: Use the **Grievance Officer.**
list: Platforms must publish the Grievance Officer's name and contact
Not happy? Appeal to the Grievance Appellate Committee

slides.title: Report it to **the authorities** too.
list: Women can get help at a One Stop Centre
slides.ref: MeitY · SOP on Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery

slides.title: Sharing private images **is a crime.**
list: Sec 66E: knowingly capturing or sharing private-area images without consent, violating privacy
Up to 3 years, or fine up to ₹2 lakh, or both
Sec 67A: publishing or sharing sexually explicit material: up to 5 years (first conviction)

slides.title: You agreed to the photo, **not to sharing.**
slides.body: If a woman agreed to an image of a private act being taken, but not to it being shared, sharing it is still voyeurism. First conviction: 1 to 3 years and fine. Repeat: 3 to 7 years and fine.

sources: IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 – Rules 3(2), 3A, updated as on 10.02.2026 (meity.gov.in)
MeitY: SOP on Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery (Nov 2025); PIB (Aug 2026)
caption:
Someone shared your private photos online? Here's what the law says. 👇

1️⃣ Complain to the platform: it must take all reasonable steps to remove or disable such content within 2 hours
2️⃣ Use the platform's Grievance Officer. Not satisfied? Appeal to the Grievance Appellate Committee within 30 days
3️⃣ Report on cybercrime.gov.in, call 1930, or go to your local police station
4️⃣ Capturing or sharing an image of someone's private area without consent, violating their privacy: up to 3 years, or fine up to ₹2 lakh, or both
5️⃣ A woman's consent to an image of a private act being captured is not consent to share it. Sharing it is voyeurism under BNS Sec 77

Source: IT Rules 2021 (Rules 3(2), 3A, as amended Feb 2026); IT Act, 2000 (Sec 66E, 67A); Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Sec 77); MeitY
